title: MindOS — landing
text: MindOS — the durable local operating system for AI agents Skip to content MindOS Product Architecture Workflow Recovery Docs Search docs ⌘K Get started ☰ Autopilot v2 · source-available (FSL-1.1-MIT) · local-first The durable local operating system for Hermes and cooperating AI agents. MindOS is a shared control plane for execution state, memory, temporal facts, handoffs, receipts, and recovery. It answers one question continuously: what is true right now, and what evidence proves it? Get started Read the architecture an IdeatorX project · MindOS Python 3.9+ · standard library only · no server to deploy · state lives in a local SQLite home The problem Agent fleets drift without execution truth. When several agents work in parallel, memory and intent live in chat transcripts, scratch files, and Git history. None of those answer the operational questions: who holds this task, is the lease still live, what evidence backs “done”, what changed while a session was dead, and how do you roll back a bad import? 01 Claims without evidence “Tests pass” in a chat message is not proof. Completions in MindOS require hash-sealed receipts stored as 0600 evidence files with sha256 recorded in the audit trail. 02 Stale ownership Dead sessions leave phantom owners. Live leases with monotonic fencing epochs reject stale processes even when the owner name still matches. 03 Unrecoverable migrations Import scripts mutate sources and leave no way back. MindOS migration is dry-run-first, byte-immutability-proven, journaled, and one-command reversible. Product model A control tower, not another cloud brain. MindOS combines five systems behind one CLI surface: autopilot.py Execution truth Tasks, claims, live leases with fencing epochs, heartbeats, retry budgets and backoff, dependency edges, impact analysis, dispatch planning, and metrics — all in SQLite. hindsight binding Shared semantic memory Hindsight remains the semantic brain through an explicit, provider-neutral binding. SQLite is the single execution authority — Hindsight is never copied into it as a second one. temporal.db Temporal facts A provenance-linked fact graph of evolving ownership, priorities, validity windows, superseded decisions, and blockers, with BM25 retrieval and temporal hybrid rerank. ops.py Recovery and portability Sealed inventories across nine source kinds, guarded stale-lease recovery, escalation, doctor health checks with FTS5 drift detection, quarantine, and cross-agent handoffs with recall digests. Architecture Four layers, one authority. Every layer exists to keep SQLite the single execution authority and to make every mutation auditable and reversible. CLI surface autopilot.py (tasks) · ops.py (fleet ops) · verify.py (end-to-end suite) Guarantees leases w/ fencing epochs · audit hash chain · receipt sealing · secret guard · FTS search SQLite home ($MINDOS_HOME) state.db — execution authority · temporal.db — optional fact-graph sidecar Migration / inventory dry-run-first manifests · rollback journal · orphan quarantine · sealed brain inventory Fail closed Ambiguity and corruption refuse with exact blockers. Absent optional sources are recorded honestly without blocking the rest. Tamper-evident audit A global hash-chained event stream; verify-chain recomputes the chain and reports tampering, with checkpoint-based truncation detection. Workflow Claim, fence, prove, complete. A real task moving through the control plane — every command below is a shipped MindOS command. mindos — task lifecycle $ python3 autopilot.py create --project Trove --title "Ship render fix" --priority P1 task created id=tsk_4f2a priority=P1 project=Trove $ python3 autopilot.py claim tsk_4f2a --owner hermes --minutes 30 lease acquired owner=hermes expires_in=30m lease_epoch=1 $ python3 autopilot.py heartbeat tsk_4f2a --owner hermes --epoch 1 --note "Running verification" heartbeat ok status=running window=15m $ python3 autopilot.py receipt tsk_4f2a --kind verification --payload '{"tests":"pass","hea

title: Documentation
text: MindOS documentation index. Everything here is grounded in the runtime repository's README, ARCHITECTURE, INSTALL, SECURITY, ROADMAP, CHANGELOG, and STABILITY docs. MindOS is the durable local operating system for Hermes and cooperating AI agents.

title: Getting started
text: MindOS is a local control plane — there is no server to deploy and no third-party packages. Python 3.9+ on macOS or Linux is the only prerequisite. git clone <repo-url> mindos cd mindos export MINDOS_HOME ="$HOME/.hermes/mindos" # any writable path works python3 autopilot.py init python3 ops.py doctor # health-check the new home init creates the SQLite schema ( state.db , plus temporal.db when the fact graph is used). All commands accept the home via MINDOS_HOME / HERMES_AUTOPILOT_HOME . Your first task python3 autopilot.py create --project Trove --title "Ship render fix" --priority P1 python3 autopilot.py claim tsk_4f2a --owner hermes --minutes 30 python3 autopilot.py heartbeat tsk_4f2a --owner hermes --note "Running verification" python3 autopilot.py receipt tsk_4f2a --kind verification --payload '{"tests":"pass"}' python3 autopilot.py complete tsk_4f2a --owner hermes --note "tests pass" Completions require a live lease and a sealed receipt — claims without evidence are rejected by policy, not by convention. Seeding an initial queue (optional) seed_current_state.py demonstrates upserting a task queue without executing any work. Point it at your own home and edit the item list first.

title: Concepts
text: Tasks and ownership A task is the unit of work: project, title, priority, status, next action, dependency edges, and an audited history. Work is claimed, not assigned — an agent acquires a live lease with a monotonic fencing epoch . Leases and fencing epochs Every lease acquisition bumps lease_epoch . A holder passes its epoch back on mutations so a stale process is rejected even when the owner name still matches. Heartbeats keep leases alive; renew extends without changing status; release hands a task back without consuming retry budget. Sealed receipts Evidence files written 0600 with a sha256 recorded in the audit trail. Completions require one — "tests pass" in chat is not proof. Temporal facts A provenance-linked graph of evolving triples with validity windows: fact-assert , facts , search-facts with BM25 retrieval and temporal hybrid rerank. Handoffs Cross-agent handoffs embed a full recall bundle (task header, dependencies, live handoff, receipts, notes) with recall digests, so the receiving agent resumes with evidence rather than a chat summary. Seam conflicts Leases prevent two agents taking the same task; seams prevent two agents editing the same checkout — an identical non-empty worktree path or the same branch in the same project is refused at claim time.

title: Architecture
text: MindOS answers one question continuously: what is true right now, and what evidence proves it? Every layer exists to keep SQLite the single execution authority and to make every mutation auditable and reversible. CLI surface autopilot.py (tasks) · ops.py (fleet ops) · verify.py (suite) Guarantees leases w/ fencing epochs · audit hash chain · receipt sealing · secret guard · FTS search SQLite home state.db (execution authority) · temporal.db (optional fact-graph sidecar) Migration/inventory dry-run-first manifests · rollback journal · orphan quarantine · sealed brain inventory Core invariants Single authority — SQLite is the execution authority; Hindsight remains a shared semantic bank and is never copied into SQLite as a second one. Fail closed — ambiguity/corruption refuses with exact blockers; absent optional sources are recorded honestly without blocking. Evidence over claims — completions require sealed receipts; audit events are digest-only where values could be sensitive. Dry-run first — destructive operations plan first, apply only on an explicit flag, journal for rollback, and re-run idempotently. Source immutability — migration reads never mutate their sources; full-fixture hash comparisons prove it. The three surfaces autopilot.py carries execution truth (tasks, leases, receipts, facts, handoffs, dispatch planning, metrics). ops.py carries fleet operations (recovery, escalation, doctor, policies, migration, brain inventory). verify.py is a self-contained end-to-end suite with failure injection, race injection, interrupted re-runs, and rollback-to-zero exercises.

title: Installation
text: Prerequisites Python 3.9+ (standard library only; no third-party packages) macOS or Linux Install git clone <repo-url> mindos cd mindos export MINDOS_HOME ="$HOME/.hermes/mindos" python3 autopilot.py init python3 ops.py doctor Health checks ops.py doctor verifies schema, lease state, audit chain, and FTS5 inverted-index health — including drift detection via fts5vocab . It is safe to run from monitoring cron before committing to a real pass. Upgrading Migration between homes is dry-run-first, journaled, and one-command reversible — see Migration . The end-to-end suite ( verify.py ) exercises interrupted re-runs and rollback to zero before any release.

title: Migration
text: Migration moves non-execution brain surfaces (memory archives, sessions, profiles, skills, cron definitions) across without turning Hindsight into a second authority, and imports execution truth into a fresh home. Sealed brain inventory python3 ops.py brain-inventory --out inventory.json python3 ops.py brain-inventory-check inventory.json # verify the seal Nine source kinds are covered — Autopilot, Hindsight binding, temporal sidecar, Claude memory sync, memory archives, sessions, profiles/skills, cron definitions — read-only, redacted, with sealed manifests. Hindsight is probed with GETs only; the shared bank is never written. Dry-run-first import python3 ops.py migrate-import … --dry-run # plan against a disposable target python3 ops.py migrate-import … # apply; journal written for rollback python3 ops.py migrate-rollback … # one-command recovery Foreign receipts are quarantined with full provenance instead of breaking foreign-key integrity. Re-runs are idempotent; source immutability is proven by full-fixture hash comparisons in the end-to-end suite.

title: Memory
text: Hindsight binding Hindsight remains the semantic brain through an explicit, provider-neutral binding. SQLite is the single execution authority — Hindsight is never copied into it as a second one. When Hindsight is unreachable, the system degrades honestly: sources are recorded absent rather than guessed at. Temporal facts python3 autopilot.py fact-assert --subject service-auth --predicate uses --object postgres-14 --source codex python3 autopilot.py facts --subject service-auth python3 autopilot.py search-facts postgres --rank Facts carry provenance, validity windows, and supersession — evolving ownership, priorities, and decisions stay queryable over time, with BM25 retrieval and temporal hybrid rerank. Notes with supersession Notes supersede rather than overwrite: the history of what was believed, when, and by whom is preserved and audited. All free-text fields pass the secret guard.

title: Tasks and receipts
text: Lifecycle Tasks move through claim → heartbeat → receipt → complete (or fail). Every transition is audited. next --claim dispatches by priority, deadline class, aging fairness, and optional critical-path tie-breaking ( --prefer-unblocking ). Leases in practice python3 autopilot.py claim tsk_4f2a --owner hermes --minutes 30 # → lease_epoch: 1 python3 autopilot.py heartbeat tsk_4f2a --owner hermes --epoch 1 python3 autopilot.py renew tsk_4f2a --owner hermes --minutes 45 python3 autopilot.py complete tsk_4f2a --owner hermes --epoch 1 --note "tests pass" A mismatch fails with lease superseded (held epoch N, current M); reclaim … . leases gives a fleet-wide live view; --all includes expired-but-still-held leases (recovery candidates). Receipts Receipts are hash-sealed evidence files (0600 + sha256 in the audit trail). Completion policy requires one, so "done" always carries proof. Failures feed retry budgets and dispatch backoff instead of disappearing. Dependencies, impact, critical path blocked-by asks what holds a task; impact walks the DAG downward; critical-path reports the longest unfinished chain — the minimum number of sequential dispatch waves needed to drain the open graph.

title: Agents and handoffs
text: The handoff protocol handoff transfers a task between agents with an objective and structured fields. The response embeds the full recall bundle — task header, dependencies, live handoff, receipts, and notes — so the receiving agent resumes with evidence rather than a chat summary. Resume: the recovery half resume is the one-call, idempotent recovery path for killed sessions: it reconstructs state and hands back the recall bundle without double-executing work. Lineage handoff-history walks the full sequence oldest → newest, showing how ownership, objective, and evidence evolved across agents. Secret guard note , supersede-note , and handoff scan their content with shape detectors (AWS keys, tokens, credential-shaped values) and block or redact by default. An explicit, itself-audited --allow-secret override exists for fleet sweeps that must locate them.

title: Recovery and rollback
text: Guarded stale-lease recovery recover sweeps stale leases with guarded, reported skips so mid-sweep claims are never wiped. leases --all previews exactly what a sweep would take. Killed sessions resume gives idempotent killed-session recovery with the full recall bundle — no double execution, no lost evidence. Migration rollback python3 ops.py migrate-import … --dry-run # plan first python3 ops.py migrate-import … # journal written python3 ops.py migrate-rollback … # target restored to pre-import state Everything destructive plans first: dry-run manifests, explicit apply flag, rollback journal, idempotent re-runs. Orphans are quarantined with provenance, never dropped. Integrity verify-chain recomputes the audit hash chain and reports tampering, with checkpoint-based truncation detection. ops.py doctor adds FTS5 drift detection via fts5vocab .

title: Security
text: What MindOS will never do (v1 contract) MindOS is a registry and evidence layer. It does not: deploy, merge, or push code; send external messages or call external APIs for writes; submit applications or take side effects on any external system; run arbitrary agent commands; or access Keychain values or credential stores. Data boundary All state lives in a local SQLite home ( $MINDOS_HOME ). The repository itself must never contain live databases, receipts, installation reports, session archives, Hindsight exports, backups, runtime artifacts, .env files, or Claude memory contents. Secret guard Every user-supplied text field passes shape detectors that block, redact, or — only under an explicit, audited override — allow credential-shaped values, so fleet sweeps can still locate them. Legacy rows sitting in live notes/handoffs are reported with the same detectors. Tamper-evident audit A global hash-chained event stream records every transition; verify-chain recomputes the chain and reports tampering. Audit events are digest-only where values could be sensitive.

title: CLI reference
text: Two entry points: autopilot.py (execution truth) and ops.py (fleet operations). All commands accept the home via MINDOS_HOME / HERMES_AUTOPILOT_HOME . autopilot.py — tasks init · create · list · claim · heartbeat · receipt · update · complete · fail release · renew · leases · transfer · resume · cancel · defer · tag · untag next --claim · plan · show · search · session-scan fact-assert · facts · search-facts · metrics · verify-chain · events · dashboard ops.py — fleet operations doctor · recover · escalate · policy brain-inventory · brain-inventory-check migrate-import · migrate-rollback verify.py — end-to-end suite Self-contained: builds disposable fixture homes and exercises every command, including failure injection, race injection, interrupted re-runs, rollback to zero, source immutability, secret-guard refusal/redaction, FTS drift, Hindsight-unavailable degradation, and cross-agent probes.

title: FAQ
text: Is MindOS open source? It is source-available under FSL-1.1-MIT — MIT-licensed after the applicable two-year change date. It is not OSI open source during the FSL restriction period. Is it a cloud service? No. There is no server to deploy. All state lives in a local SQLite home; MindOS never sends external messages or writes to external APIs. Does it replace Git? No. Git remains the right tool for code. MindOS is the operational layer Git was never designed to be — leases, receipts, recovery — and it complements rather than replaces your repos. What if Hindsight is down? The system degrades honestly: the binding is probed, absence is recorded as absent , and execution truth in SQLite continues uninterrupted. Hindsight is semantic memory, never a second authority. Honest limitations Leases prevent task collisions but seams (shared worktrees/branches) are refused at claim time, not merged safely. The secret guard is shape-based, not a general credential scanner. Packaging and single-command bootstrap are on the roadmap, not shipped.

title: Roadmap
text: Honest status as of August 2026. Nothing is claimed as done unless it ships in the runtime repository with verify coverage. Shipped (v1) Task registry with live leases, fencing epochs, retry budgets, backoff, dependency edges, impact analysis, dispatch planning, and metrics. Hash-chained audit stream with tamper detection ( verify-chain ). Sealed receipts and approval receipts (0600 files + sha256). Notes with supersession; provenance-linked temporal fact graph. Cross-agent handoffs with recall digests; session retention ( sessions-prune ). Secret guard (block/redact/audited override) over all free-text fields. Doctor health checks incl. FTS5 drift detection via fts5vocab. Dry-run-first migration layer: inventory, import, orphan-receipt quarantine, rollback journal, idempotent re-runs, source immutability proofs. End-to-end brain inventory across nine source kinds with sealed manifests. Next Hourly control tower — report task changes on a schedule without executing work. Cross-agent probe hardening — broader post-install recall/handoff probes. Policy expansion — more project policies gating automatic side effects per client. Parallel MindOS home — verified parallel installation with one-command rollback. Packaging — single-command bootstrap and versioned release notes. Non-goals Cloud hosting, external messaging, code deployment, or becoming a second semantic-memory authority alongside Hindsight.
